title: PQID-Bench: A Validation-Aware Benchmark Suite for Quantum-Program Generation
description:
Overview

PQID-Bench v1.0.0 is a frozen, validation-aware benchmark, evidence bundle, and reproducibility suite for evaluating quantum-program generation. It was derived from PQID v1.0.2 through explicit validation, cleanliness, and benchmark-readiness rules rather than by flattening every source record into one test set. The deposit is self-contained: it includes materialized training, validation, and test JSONL files, so users do not need to download or reconstruct the benchmark from the parent PQID dataset.

PQID-Bench supports three main uses: reproducing the released 21-model evaluation, inspecting its prompt-level evidence and robustness audits, and evaluating additional model outputs under the same frozen scoring contract.

What the release contains

  • A 734-row clean quantum-program generation population: 415 strict rows and 319 extended rows.
  • A deterministic 514/66/154 train/validation/test split in data/splits/, including 154 held-out prompts representing 144 evaluator-facing target signatures.
  • Canonical responses and evaluator traces for 21 named model routes over all 154 test prompts (3,234 model-prompt cells).
  • Three retrieval-copy baselines; ordered-operand and parameter-aware replay audits; clustered inferential and sensitivity analyses; and a three-run stochastic-repeatability audit over 72 signature-unique prompts.
  • Evaluator and structural-predicate implementations, exact manifests, SHA-256 checksums, software bills of materials, documentation, and scripts that regenerate the public analytical outputs.

Measurement nomenclature

  • E - Python execution: the generated response executes in the pinned Python/Qiskit environment and yields an extractable quantum circuit.
  • A - quantum assembly execution: E=1 and the extracted circuit serializes successfully to OpenQASM 3 under the frozen evaluator. This is an assembly-admissibility layer; it does not mean that the emitted OpenQASM program was run by a separate quantum-assembly runtime.
  • M^sig - reference-signature recovery: the executable output agrees with the frozen target on qubit count, classical-bit count, and the complete operation-type count map. Scalar counted-operation agreement follows from count-map equality in this release and is also reported as a diagnostic.
  • ES-Gap - Execution-Structure Gap: the pooled Python-execution rate minus the pooled reference-signature recovery rate.
  • AS-Gap - Assembly-Structure Gap: the pooled quantum-assembly rate minus the pooled reference-signature recovery rate. On the frozen panel, it is the assembly-admissible part of the ES-Gap.

Frozen headline evidence

Across the complete 21 x 154 matrix, 2,950 of 3,234 outputs satisfy E (91.22%), 2,944 satisfy A (91.03%), and 1,703 satisfy M^sig (52.66%). The ES-Gap is therefore 1,247/3,234 = 38.56 percentage points. Only six executable outputs fail the assembly layer, whereas the AS-Gap is 1,241/3,234 = 38.37 points and retains 99.52% of the ES-Gap. The observed separation is consequently concentrated between operational admissibility and measured structural recovery, not between Python execution and OpenQASM 3 serialization.

Python package and first use

The maintained command-line and Python interface is the separately versioned pqid-bench package. This Zenodo record archives the exact pqid-bench 1.1.2 wheel published on PyPI. The current separately distributed pqid-bench 1.2.0 package adds authenticated compact benchmark acquisition to the numerical summaries, comparisons, interactive Plotly reporting, live-model workflows, and prospective O6 link without changing the frozen benchmark data, responses, or scoring contract.

python -m pip install "pqid-bench==1.2.0"
pqid-bench download --version 1.0.0
pqid-bench verify RELEASE_DIR --full
pqid-bench reproduce --release-dir RELEASE_DIR --format text

Install pqid-bench[visualization]==1.2.0 to create a standalone dashboard with pqid-bench dashboard. Use pqid-bench evaluate and pqid-bench compare for R-style numerical summaries and run comparisons, pqid-bench run-model for explicitly authorized live provider testing, and pqid-bench replay for isolated Docker-backed execution of generated code. Full instructions are available in the documentation.

Version crosswalk

  • Frozen benchmark and evidence release: PQID-Bench 1.0.0.
  • Current Python interface: pqid-bench 1.2.0 on PyPI.
  • Archived Python interface in this deposit: the pqid-bench 1.1.2 wheel, byte-identical to PyPI; its venue-neutral source tree is included in the frozen ZIP.
  • Evaluator implementation: pqid-bench-evaluator-1.1.0-safe-builtins.
  • Structural predicate: pqid-bench-reference-signature-1.0.0-count-map.
  • Reproducible evaluator container: ghcr.io/elias-abebe-gasparini/pqid-bench-evaluator:1.0.0.

Interpretive, safety, and licensing boundaries

Reference-signature, ordered-operand, or parameter-aware agreement does not by itself establish unitary, measurement-distribution, or semantic equivalence. Conversely, signature disagreement establishes disagreement with the measured frozen target but not general physical invalidity. Live provider evaluation transmits benchmark prompts to the selected third party and requires explicit user acknowledgement. Generated code should be replayed only through the pinned Docker evaluator, not in the caller process.

Benchmark-authored documentation, metadata, and aggregate analyses are licensed under CC BY 4.0; package and evaluator code are MIT-licensed. Source-derived rows retain row-level provenance and upstream licensing obligations. Unpublished manuscript source and manuscript-facing publication derivatives are intentionally excluded from this public release.
